🔥 The fire settles. the man in his 20s has been quiet all evening, and now everyone knows why. "A crow that watches too long and blinks too little — I put it down today." "Its shadow detaches from the branch-shadow and slides across the ground toward you — a straight black lane, growing. The bird hasn't moved. The shadow has." "It climbs, laughing in a dead voice — out of spear reach, watching." A beat of silence, then the questions come all at once. the person in their 30s, with calloused knuckles, the baker asks "Say that again — slower." Nathan mutters "The fire feels smaller now."
